Veeregowda vs Mahadevaswamy S.M on 28 August, 2024
Kabc020187792021
 Before The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal
 Court Of Small Causes, At Bengaluru. (Scch-25) 
 - : Present:- 
 Smt. Prakriti Kalyanpur, B.A(L),Ll.B., Ll.M.
 Xxiii Additional Small Causes Judge, Bengaluru. 
 Dated This The 28Th Day Of August 2024 
 Mvc No.2889/2021
 Petitioner:  Sri. Veeregowda  S/o. Kyathaiah,
 Aged about 42 years,
 R/at No.87, 11th Main Road,
 Near Anibasant School,
 Srinivasanagara,
 Bangalore - 560 091.
 And also R/at Ajjanahalli  Village at Post,
 Magdi Taluk,
 Ramanagara District. 
 (By Shivalingaiah K.P.,
 Advocate/s.)
 V/S  RESPONDENTS: 1. Sri. Mahadevaswamy  S.M.
 S/o Mahdeva,
 Aged Major,
 R/at No.19, 2nd Floor,
 3rd Cross, Hegganahalli,
 Peenya 2nd stage,
 Bangalore - 560 058.
 SCCH - 25 2 MVC 2889/2021  (RC owner of the Ashok  Leyland Goods bearing  Reg.No.KA-02-AH-5998)
 (By Smt. Nagarathana,
 Advocate.) 
 2. The Manager  Reliance General Insurance,

1  Office at 4/3-1 and 3/2 M.,
 11th Main, 3rd Block,
 Jayanagar,
 Bangalore - 560 061.
 (Insurer of the Ashok  Leyland Goods bearing  Reg.No.KA-02-AH-5998)
 Policy  No.992492023340008448  Policy period from  21.08.2020 to 20.08.2021)
 (By Smt. Aruna V, Advocate.)
 ......
 JUDGMENT The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road accident dated 12.06.2021.
2. The case of the Petitioner in brief is that:
On 12.06.2021 at about 05.45pm, while the Petitioner was proceeding in a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-HX- 6702 from Andrahalli to Srinivasanagara to go to his home and when he reached Maseedi Cross, near Hegganahalli ground,
Andrahalli Main Road, a Ashok Leyland Goods bearing No.KA-02-AH-5998 came from opposite Road, driven by its driver with a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life and dashed the petitioner's motorcycle. Due to the terrible impact, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries. 
3. It is the further case of the Petitioner that, immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Jai Maruthi Hospital, provided first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Sun Orthopedic Hospital,
Mattikere, Bangalore wherein he was admitted as an inpatient for a period of 16 days, underwent several clinical and radiological examination and taken treatment for the injuries. So far he has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, nourishment and transportation expenses. 
4. It is the further case of the Petitioner that, prior to the date of accident he was hale and healthy,
doing self employment of Driver work and earning Rs.20,000/- per month. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he cannot attend his work permanently, resulting in loss of earning and he is put to great financial hardship and untold misery. The accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-02-AH-5998 and the Peenya Traffic Police have filed charge sheet against the driver in Cr.No.56/2021 punishable u/Sec.279, 337 of IPC. The 1st Respondent being the RC owner and the 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. 
Hence, this petition. 
Veeregowda vs Mahadevaswamy S.M on 28 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154966968/
2 5. In response to notice issued by this tribunal, the Respondents appeared through their respective counsels but, respondent No.2 alone filed written statement. 
6. The objections of the Respondent No.2:
The averments made in the petition are not within the knowledge of the respondent. 
It has denied the issuance of policy in respect of the vehicle Ashok Leyland goods vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AH-5998. There is non compliance of Sec.134(c) of MV Act so this respondent is not liable to indemnify the 1st respondent against the alleged cause of action. The insured has knowingly entrusted the vehicle to the Driver who was not having valid DL and also did not have valid FC to the vehicle. The Respondent insurer has further denied the manner of accident, petitioner's age,
occupation, income and other details of the Petitioner and has sought for dismissal of the petition. 
7. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:-
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Ashok Leyland Goods Carrier bearing Reg.No.KA-02- AH-5998 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries? 
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation? If so, what is the quantum? From whom payable?
3 . What order or award? 
8. The Petitioner in order to prove his case, has examined himself as PW.1 and has got marked 12 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.12. He has also examined Mr. Kusumesha M. - MRO/Technician in Sun Orthopedic Hospital as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.13 to P.16. Dr.Nagaraj B.N. was examined as PW.3 and got marked Exs.P.17 & 18. On the other side, the Respondent No.2 has got examined Mr.Nagesh Kumar H.B - MRD, Jaimaruthi Hospital as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1. It has also examined Mr. Govindaiah H. - Superintendent, Rajajinagar RTO as RW.2 and got marked Exs.R.2 &
R.3. Ms.Thrishi P.S.
- Legal Manager at Respondent No.2 got examined as RW.3 and got marked Exs.R.4 & R.5.
9. Heard the arguments of the learned counsels for both the parties. 
10. On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows:-
 Issue No.1: In the affirmative,
 Issue No.2: In the affirmative,
 Issue No.3: As per the final order,
Veeregowda vs Mahadevaswamy S.M on 28 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154966968/
3  for the following:-
 REASONS  11. Issue No.1:
In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Ashok Leyland Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-02-AH-5998 the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and has got marked 9 documents as per Exs.P.1 to 9. PW.1 has reiterated the averments of the petition in his affidavit in lieu of his chief examination. The Respondent No.2 has denied the manner of accident and also denied the negligence and rash driving by the driver. 
Further contended that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the petitioner himself. In the cross-examination of PW.1, he has admitted 3 days delay in filing of complaint. On the day of complaint, the police have seized the offending vehicle, gave notice u/Sec.133 of MV Act and also received reply. The petitioner has also got examined Kasumesha M. - MRO/Technician in Sun Orthopedic Hospital as PW.2 and got marked authorization letter, police intimation, MLC register extract and case sheet pertaining to the petitioner as per Exs.P.13 to P.16. During the cross examination of PW.2 he has stated that in the police intimation and MLC register extract there is no mention of which vehicle caused the accident. 
12. The FIR was registered on 15.06.2021 at about 9.00am on the complaint of petitioner given by his wife after Four days at Exs.P.1 & 2. Ex.P.3 is the wound certificate giving details of accident which occurred on 12.06.2021 at about 5.45pm near Andrahalli Main Road. Ex.P.4 is the spot mahazar, shows the details and spot of the accident conducted on 15.06.2021 at 11.00am to 12.00pm. Ex . P.5 sketch shows the accident spot. Ex.P.6 MVA report shows that petitioner's vehicle damaged to its front head light mask, front safety guard become bent at right side and the offending vehicle also damaged to its front right side bumper. Exs . P.7 & 8 are the notice sent to the owner of the offending vehicle and reply to the said notice by the owner. Ex.P.9 is the charge sheet filed against the driver of the offending Ashok Leyland Lorry after thorough investigation. In this regard the respondent No.2 has examined Dr.Nagesh Kumar H.B. - MRD, Jaimaruthi Hospital as RW.1 and got marked copy of MLC register extract as Ex.R.1. During the cross examination of RW.1 he has stated that, the petitioner came to their hospital immediately after the accident since the spot of accident is in front of the hospital. Further he stated that the petitioner was under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident. However the other documents on record like mahazar and sketch show that the Ashok Leyland Lorry came to the right side of the Road. This shows absence of any negligence on the part of the petitioner even if he was under the influence of the alcohol. Therefore,
the respondent No.2 has failed to prove that the accident was caused because of the petitioner being under the influence of alcohol. On the other hand, from the documents on record, the Tribunal holds that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Ashok Leyland Goods Carrier bearing Reg.No.KA-02-AH-5998. Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative. 
13. Issue No.2:-
Veeregowda vs Mahadevaswamy S.M on 28 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154966968/
4 In order to prove the injuries and disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner has produced the Wound Certificate at Ex.P.3. As per Ex.P.3, the Petitioner has sustained (i) comminuted displaced  proximal tibia fracture, proximal fibula fracture right which are grievous in nature. 
14. The Petitioner got examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW.3 and got marked recent clinical reports and recent X- ray at Exs.P.17 & 18. In his chief examination he has stated the details of the fracture suffered by the petitioner, the treatment undergone by him, the difficulties suffered by him while doing day today activities and has assessed the disability and stability and has fixed right lower limb disability at 40% and whole body disability at 13%. During the cross examination of PW.3, he has stated that he is not a treated doctor. The mobilization of joints will be advised at the time of discharge. The regular usage of the limb will improve the muscle strength and range of movement of the particular limb. Now the petitioner is using the limb without any support because the fracture is good in alignment. 
15. From the evidence of PW.3 it can be seen that the disability being suffered by the petitioner will impact his work. PW.3 has assessed the total disability of the right lower limb at 40% and to the whole body at 13%. The petitioner is a Car Driver who needs his leg regularly for his driving work. 
Therefore, the court deems it fit to consider the whole body disability at 13%. 
Monthly income:
16. The Petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, he was a Car driver and getting salary of Rs.20,000/- per month. In this regard he has not examined any witness nor produced any Bank statement and any other documents in support of it. The accident occurred in the year 2021. 
Therefore, this Tribunal deems it fit to fix the notional income at Rs.15,000/- per month. 
17. At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 42 years as could be made out from Ex.P.12/Notarized copy of Aadhar Card. He was hale and healthy before the accident. Keeping all the above things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:-
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:- 
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at Jai Maruthi Hospital and thereafter at Sun Orthopedic Hospital, Mattikere, Bangalore admitted as an inpatient and discharged with advice to take follow up treatment. In this regard, he has produced Ex.P.10 Discharge summary of Sun Orthopedic Hospital. Considering that the nature of injuries he has undergone is grievous, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.70,000/- under this head. 
ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES: 
The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- towards hospitalization,
medical expenses, extra nourishment, conveyance and other miscellaneous expenses etc., In this regard, he has produced medical bills as per Ex.P.11 for a sum of Rs.1,37,337/-. There is no contrary Veeregowda vs Mahadevaswamy S.M on 28 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154966968/
5 evidence to these bills from the respondent No.2. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to the said amount under this head. 
iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:-
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries. The petitioner has taken treatment at Sun Orthopedic Hospital which can be made out from Ex.P.10 Discharge summary. Therefore, considering the nature of injuries and duration of treatment it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least one month time for recovering from the injuries sustained by him. Hence, he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.15,000/- under this head.
iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:- 
On perusal of Ex.P.12/Aadhar Card, the date of birth of the petitioner is 01.07.1979 and the date of accident is 12.06.2021. Therefore, as on the date of the accident the Petitioner's age is 42 years. As per the dictum laid down in Sarala Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 14. As such the petitioner is entitled to Rs.3,27,600/-. (Rs.15,000/- x 12 x 13% x 14 = Rs.3,27,600/- ).
 (v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:- 
The Petitioner was aged about 42 years at the time of accident. He has sustained grievous injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 13%
functional disability. The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life. 
Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts. Therefore,
considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered, a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head. 
(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES: 
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospitals, admitted for 3 days as an inpatient and discharged with advise. However, during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses. Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/-
under this head. 
(vii) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES: 
As per the version of PW.3, the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants and the estimate of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/-. In this regard the petitioner or the PW.3 have not produced any estimation letter. Therefore,
looking to the earlier treatment cost and nature of injuries, evidence on record, it Veeregowda vs Mahadevaswamy S.M on 28 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154966968/
6 appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.30,000/- is awarded under this head. 
18. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.70,000/-
2. Medical expenses Rs.1,37,337/-
3. Loss of income during laid up Rs.15,000/- period 4. Loss of future income Rs.3,27,600/-
5 . Loss of future amenities and Rs.20,000/- happiness 6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/- nourishment charges 7. Future Medical Expenses Rs.30,000/-
TOTAL Rs.6,19,937/-
If it is rounded off it comes around Rs.6,20,000/- and same is awarded under different heads to the Petitioner. 
LIABILITY 19. The respondent No.2 has contended that the driver of the offending vehicle did not have a valid DL at the time of accident and the insured has committed breach of contract of insurance. In order to prove the same, they examined Mr. Govindaiah H. Superintendent, Rajajinagar RTO as RW.2 and got marked authorization letter and DL extract of Mahadevaswamy SM as per Exs.R.2 and R.3.
During the cross examination of RW.2 stated that the DL issued to the driver of the Lorry is for motorcycle with gear, LMV, LMV-TR but, the driver Mahadevaswamy is not possessing a DL for heavy goods vehicle. Further the Ashok Leyland Dost vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AH-5998 is a LMV vehicle and the driver was entitled to drive the same. The unladen weight was 1390kg. At the time of accident the driver of the offending vehicle had a valid DL to drive the offending vehicle. In order to prove their defence the Respondent No.2 got examined its Legal Manager as RW.1, who filed affidavit in lieu of her chief examination reiterating the objections. She got marked Exs.R.4 & 5 Authorization letter & copy of insurance policy. During her cross- examination, she has admitted that the vehicle number is mentioned at Ex.R.1. Therefore, the respondents have failed to prove their defence. The Respondents being the Owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner. However, as the policy existed as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2/insurer has to indemnify the respondent No.1/insured and to pay compensation awarded to the petitioner. The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.15,00,000/- but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.6,20,000/- with interest @ 6% per annum Veeregowda vs Mahadevaswamy S.M on 28 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154966968/
7 from the date of petition till its realization. Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed. Accordingly,
I answer Issue No.2 in the affirmative. 
20. Issue No.3:
For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this court proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER The petition is allowed with cost. 
 The Petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.6,20,000/- (Rupees Six Lakhs and Twenty Thousand only) from the Respondents along with interest at 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount. The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the petitioner. 
However, the Respondent No.2/Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award. 
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner by way of e-payment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per rules. 
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-. Draw decree accordingly. 
(Typed to my dictation directly on the computer by the Stenographer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court on this the 28th Day of August 2024). 
(PRAKRITI KALYANPUR) XXIII ASCJ & ACJM, Bangalore.
